At the user's request, checked whether arXiv:2508.17627 was held. It was — but
only as its ACL 2026 camera-ready (`doi:10.18653/v1/2026.acl-long.1239`,
"The Evolution of Thought", the RCP/RCPD paper), with an empty `arxiv_id` and
no alias tying the preprint id to it. The generated section above is the
run_daily record written at ingest time and still names the file, not the
paper; the reading below is what the record now holds.

Reviewing it against the PDF turned up two things worth keeping.

**The stored ACL reading had corrupted numbers.** Its `results` field reported
"AIME24: 72.45 vs. 72.34 Full" (both are 72.22 — the two are equal), quoted
64.21 as a GPQA-D accuracy when it is that cell's RPCR (accuracy is 64.65),
and claimed AIME25 "67.78 vs 63.33 Full, +4.45pp above Full" when RCPD and
Full both score 63.33. Two further baseline comparisons cited values absent
from the rows they named. The qualitative half of that reading was accurate
throughout — the 97.3% in-basin figure, the KL formulation, the rank signal,
the iso-compute BF design — so the corruption is confined to transcribing a
dense results table. Whether other readings of table-heavy papers share it has
not been checked. **These wrong numbers had already been quoted back to the
user in analysis before the check.**

**The two versions of the paper differ in a way that matters.** arXiv v2
(13 Jan 2026) carries a training-based S-GRPO row in Table 1 that the ACL
camera-ready removed, along with the sentence conceding the comparison:
S-GRPO reaches 77.30 on AIME24/Qwen3-8B with 8,810 tokens against RCPD's
72.22 with 9,958, while RCPD wins on GPQA-D (64.65 vs 55.40). The published
version drops S-GRPO from the baseline list, the table and the text, leaving
Full/No-Think/BF/DEER — so a reader of the camera-ready alone cannot see that
the paper was beaten on AIME24 by a method it had measured. v2's appendices
also carry material the reading should have: the actual RCPD stopping rules
are four hand-set rank thresholds (R_t <= 5; the ladder [10, 50, 100, 1000];
<= 20 over 3 steps; <= 50 over 6 steps), and Appendix F reports a
counterfactual injection experiment in which 49 of 64 trials adopt an injected
wrong intermediate answer rather than recovering the correct one — direct
evidence that post-RCP computation rationalizes instead of re-verifying.

Re-collecting the ACL record was considered first and is a no-op: both
`run_daily.py:303` and `render.py:120` skip any paper that already has a
summary, so nothing re-queues an item that has been read. The route taken
instead was to file the arXiv v2 PDF through `inbox/`, read it as a document,
and merge. Render's `reconcile_identifiers` flagged the two records as
contested on its own before the merge was asked for.

**Two things about `dedupe merge` that cost time and should not cost it
again.** First, when both records carry a reading the survivor keeps its own
and the absorbed one is deleted — so survivor and absorbed are not
interchangeable here, and naming the old record as survivor would have
destroyed the correction and kept the corrupted reading. The CLI says this
plainly; `merge_records`' own docstring contradicts it, claiming the second
reading "is kept where it is rather than silently dropped", which the code at
`dedupe.py:154` does not do. Second, `merge` accepts a record's *filename*
form (`doi-10-18653-...`) because `load_paper` resolves it, but `SeenStore`
is keyed on the canonical form (`doi:10.18653/...`), so a merge named that way
reports `problems: []` and `keys_repointed: 0` and repoints nothing — the
identifiers stay pointing at a record that has just been deleted. Passing the
canonical ids gave `keys_repointed: 2`.

The surviving record is `local:7c50df663462f26b`, carrying both identifiers
(arXiv 2508.17627v2 and the ACL DOI), venue ACL, the ACL author list, and the
reading of v2. The id is the hand-filed form rather than a DOI form; that is
the cost of making the corrected reading the survivor.

Not done, and left as a question: whether to record the version difference as
a finding, and whether to audit other table-heavy readings for the same
transcription failure. The 10 pending concept tasks are the stale-definition
tail and were deliberately left alone.
